Record Class Address

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
com.trevlar.slotkit.api.window.Address
public record Address(com.trevlar.slotkit.window.OwnerRef owner, com.trevlar.slotkit.window.Token token, KindTag kind) extends Record
One value that names any addressable thing (a vanilla slot, a created slot, a panel element or a panel itself), so the engine can resolve every behavior by address without asking what kind it is.

The four shapes

  vanilla slot   : RootOwner(family, scope)              + IndexToken(i)    + VANILLA_SLOT
  created slot   : NestedOwner(RootOwner(family,scope), RegToken(panel)) + DeclToken(id) + CREATED_SLOT
  panel element  : NestedOwner(RootOwner(family,scope), RegToken(panel)) + DeclToken(id) + PANEL_ELEMENT
  panel itself   : RootOwner(family, scope)              + RegToken(panel) + PANEL
The old slot-only SlotAddress(family, index) is exactly the first line.

Identity contract

Equality is over (owner, token, kind), from the record. KindTag takes part so a panel and a slot at the same coordinate never collide, and a created slot and a panel element with the same declaration id stay distinct. The address holds no live object, so two addresses naming the same thing are equal and interchangeable: safe to keep in a static map, compare, and pass across the client/server boundary as a key. The same thing rebuilds to an equal address after a reopen, because its sources are deterministic (vanilla's menu index, the consumer's panel and declaration ids, the registration order).

Minting one

  • a created slot: createdSlot(SlotGroupId.Created, int), from the group's id (ParityGroup.idOf, CreatedSlots.groupId, SlotGroupId.created) and the slot's index in the group;
  • a vanilla slot: from the live slot, where an operation or veto has it, or by its place in a menu type's slot list, menuSlot(MenuType, int).
Panel and panel-element addresses are no longer minted (MenuKit names its panels by Panel.id()), but parse(String) still reads the text 6.x saved for them. The value-level factories below the public ones are the library's plumbing and are @ApiStatus.Internal.

Saving one

asString() is a stable text form to save a choice about one thing under, parse(String) reads it back, and CODEC is the same form for codec-based config. Never save an address's internals: their shape may change, the text form's meaning does not.

Sources

Where the value-level factories get their parts: the creative tab from OwnerScope.tab(BuiltInRegistries.CREATIVE_MODE_TAB.getKey(selectedTab)) (client tier); a created slot's DeclToken from its (groupId, localIndex) registration coordinate; a composite container's backing from OwnerScope.sub(...).

An OwnerScope.Tab scope is client tier only, since the active tab lives on the screen, never the menu. The value itself has no notion of tier and cannot enforce this, so the engine's tier check has to reject a Tab-scoped address in server-tier resolution, and mint sites must respect it.

    • menuSlot

      public static Address menuSlot(net.minecraft.world.inventory.MenuType<?> type, int index)
      Slot index of menu.slots on every menu of type: the menu-based form of a vanilla slot's address. A panel registered once for a menu type holds this, since a slot's container-based address (what SlotRef.address() gives for a chest or a shulker box) names one particular box. Not equal to that container-based address, so behaviors keyed on a slot's address don't see this one; it is for placing slots (SlotElement.builder().slot(Address)).

    • playerInventory

      public static Address playerInventory(int index)
      Slot index of the viewing player's own inventory, the same slot on every screen that shows it, survival's and creative's included: 0 to 8 the hotbar, 9 to 35 the main grid, 36 to 39 armor (feet to head), 40 the offhand. Equal to SlotRef.address() for that slot, so a rule declared on it at init holds wherever the slot is. Since 2.1.0.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - for an index outside 0 to 40
